learning_objective: 🎯 Break out of the right-angled triangle! Learn to measure angles in Radians, explore trigonometric functions on a Unit Circle, and master the identities for any angle size.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Angles aren't just measured in degrees. A Radian is the angle subtended at the center of a circle by an arc equal in length to the radius. The magic conversion rule is: $\pi \text{ radians} = 180^\circ$.

By placing a circle with radius 1 on a graph, any point on the circle is $(\cos \theta, \sin \theta)$. The ASTC Rule (All Sin Tan Cos or 'Add Sugar To Coffee') tells you which trig functions are positive in the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th quadrants respectively.

Trigonometric functions repeat their values at regular intervals (they are periodic). The graphs of $\sin x$ and $\cos x$ look like endless waves that repeat every $2\pi$ radians, while $\tan x$ repeats every $\pi$ radians.

You will unlock powerful formulas to calculate the trig values of combined angles, like $\sin(A \pm B)$, $\cos(A \pm B)$, and the C-D formulas. These are the tools used to simplify massive trigonometric equations.

fun_activity.title: 🧭 The 'Add Sugar To Coffee' Compass
fun_activity.instructions: Draw a large '+ ' sign to make 4 quadrants. Write 'A' (All) in the 1st, 'S' (Sin) in the 2nd, 'T' (Tan) in the 3rd, and 'C' (Cos) in the 4th. This simple phrase 'Add Sugar To Coffee' will forever save you from guessing whether a trig value should be positive or negative based on its angle!

exam_tips: 📌 Always convert degrees to radians before applying calculus or advanced algebra formulas ($Radian = Degree \times \frac{\pi}{180}$).
📌 Memorize the double angle formulas (e.g., $\cos 2x = \cos^2 x - \sin^2 x$); they are the most frequently used substitutions in long derivation questions.
📌 The ranges of $\sin x$ and $\cos x$ are strictly $[-1, 1]$. If your calculated sine value is 2.5, you've made an error!
quick_recap: ⭐ The relation between arc length ($l$), radius ($r$), and angle in radians ($\theta$) is $l = r\theta$.
⭐ The formula for $\cos(A+B)$ has a MINUS sign: $\cos A \cos B - \sin A \sin B$.
